newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse says no plans to discuss offers.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse says no plans to discuss offers.

text.p: Westinghouse Electric Corp has no plans to enter into discussions with two French companies interested in acquiring its nuclear-energy and power-generation businesses, a spokesman said Tuesday.

Westinghouse spokesman Kevin Ramundo was responding to a report in the Tuesday editions of French daily Les Echos. The article said nuclear engineering company Framatome Connectors invited Westinghouse to discuss the possible acquisition of its nuclear energy business, and that GEC Alsthom did the same for the power-generation unit.
The report said the offers were made in early August, and the French companies had not received an answer from Westinghouse.
Ramundo said there were no plans to discuss the offers with the interested parties.
"We are not in discussions; we are proceeding with plans to separate the company. Our focus is on building (our industrial businesses) into the strongest competitive position," he added.
Westinghouse is scheduled to complete the separation of its media and industrial operations next month.
